newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby league-ARL backer dismisses Super League.
newsitem.headline: Rugby league-ARL backer dismisses Super League.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL) on Friday launched a 12-team competition for 1997 after one of its major sponsors dismissed media baron Rupert Murdoch's rival Super League as "a series of exhibition matches".
ARL chief executive John Quayle said the ARL premiership would begin on March 14 in direct competition with a likely 10-team Super League in Australia.
The ARL lost eight clubs to Super League, which last week won an appeal against court orders banning it until 2000 and is now free to start in Australia for the first time next year.
Geoffrey Cousins, chief executive of the ARL's major backer, pay television operator Optus Vision, told a news conference Super League was "a make-up competition".
"The (ARL's) Optus Cup is seven out of the top 10 teams as they finished this year," Cousins said.
"This is the real thing. The other one is a series of exhibition matches and I don't really think, with all due respect, that exhibition matches are what people really want," he said.
While the full draw for next year will not be released until next week, Quayle said the season will kick off with a match between Parramatta and North Sydney.

Champions Manly and St George, who met in last month's ARL grand final in the last season to feature all 20 clubs in the same competition, will resume hostilities in the second round of matches the following weekend.
The start of the ARL's 1996 season was delayed by three weeks because of a long-running legal battle with Super League.
